text:
maya: Quick sync — I ran the audit-coverage report for the last 2 sprints. We still have blind spots in multiple services: API gateway (proxy auth events), auth (refresh/token lifecycle), Console (org admin actions), Billing (invoice export), and Runtime (model request metadata). Spreadsheet here: https://redwood.internal/reports/audit-coverage-2956789000.csv. Need to validate customer-facing audit evidence for SOC/PCI. Who can pick up triage?

samir: I can take api-gateway + auth. What's the canonical schema we want? Does the report include sample events I can use?

maya: Yes — the report includes samples in the last column but the schemas diverge a lot. High-level gaps: actor id naming (actor.id vs user_id), missing request_id on billing exports, inconsistent resource/target fields, and we don't always log KMS usage (key id / encryption context). Also RBAC change events (role grants, revokes) are inconsistently emitted.

olga: I can own Console + Billing. For billing exports specifically: missing request_id, no delegated_user, and we don't log the cmk id when a customer uses a CMK during export. That breaks evidence validation.

alex: Runtime team here — we currently emit model_id and session_id only. To satisfy compliance we need request_origin, dataset_hash, and KMS encryption_context (when model inputs are encrypted).

sec-bot: Created task INTF-8345 "Audit: add request_id to billing export" and assigned to olga.

samir: For the gateway, an immediate standard envelope would be easiest. Proposal:```json
{
  "event_ts": "",
  "request_id": "",
  "actor": { "id": "", "type": "" },
  "action": "",
  "resource": { "type": "", "id": "" },
  "kms": { "key_id": "", "encryption_context": "" }
}
```That would allow downstream validation and mapping. I'll open a schema PR w/ examples.

maya: Good. Also we need a short compatibility doc for customers (many expect event.actor.id). We'll standardize naming and publish a migration mapping for older fields.

olga: Tentative owners: samir (gateway + auth), olga (console + billing), alex (runtime). I can build a small validation harness to replay events against customer expectations and flag missing fields.

alex: We need infra coordination for KMS context names — current variants across services: kms_key_id, key_id, cmk_id. Can we standardize?

maya: Standardize on kms.key_id and kms.encryption_context. Add to the spec and enforce in the validation harness.

samir: I'll draft a schema PR and include migration notes mapping old fields to the new names. Will add sample ingestion tests.

olga: Timeline? We should aim for an MVP (schema + tests + harness) by next Wednesday so we can demo for compliance reviewers.

maya: Plan: owners break out tasks and link them to an INTF epic. I'll create INTF-8399 and add owners + timeline. Drop PR links here when ready.

samir: @sec-bot can you attach the coverage CSV snapshot to the PRs and tickets?

sec-bot: Attached /reports/audit-coverage-2956789000.csv to INTF-8345 and INTF-8399.

alex: Quick Q on PII — do we want to redact emails/phone numbers in logs? Runtime will redact full emails and SSN-like strings before emitting. For customer evidence we can surface hashed identifiers (salted per-customer).

maya: Policy: logs must not contain raw PII. For evidence, use hashed values + per-customer salt; include the hash algorithm in the event metadata. Add that to spec.

olga: I'll add a ticket checklist: sample events, canonical schema diff, KMS field standardization, redaction rules, unit + integration tests, and customer-facing docs.

maya: Thanks all. We'll reconvene at Friday standup for status. :thumbsup:
